## Why

*Proposed.* A grok row whose login fails mid-run stops that run for the owner. `ork vendor out grok` (no `--until`) holds every grok row out across restarts, so each role falls back to its next row; the matrices still name grok first and should say so.

Open owner questions (the implementer asks them with `adj ask` first):

- Q1 (`vendors.grok-cutover`): how is grok retired? (a) *recommended*: on 2026-12-08 the orchestrator runs `ork vendor out grok --reason "accounts end 2026-12-09"`; this slice moves every grok row in ork's matrix after its Claude or Codex fallback and marks it retired with the date; slicer's matrix gets the same change through an item filed in slicer. (b) delete the grok rows outright.
- Q2 (`vendors.grok-local-after-cutover`): does `grok-local` still run without the grok account? (a) *recommended*: probe once (`grok-local` on a read-only task with the cloud login signed out is not possible to test before the date; instead read the launcher and the grok CLI's auth requirements, and ask the owner). (b) treat grok-local as retired with grok.
